meta.label: Off-grid power systems
tradeoffLabels: cheapest price for the storage capacity you get
most charge cycles and the longest warranty before the battery needs replacing
meta.attribution: Covers real, purchasable off-grid power systems sold into the US market, from portable all-in-one power stations you can carry home and plug in the same day, to bare 12V lithium batteries for a self-built system, whole-home batteries from Tesla, Enphase, FranklinWH and Generac, and whole-home hybrid inverters that need a licensed installer and days of wiring, plus two routes that are not a product purchase: hiring a NABCEP-certified installer to design and build a custom system, and staying on the electric grid where it already reaches a property. Cost is scored only where a manufacturer publishes a fixed listed or sale price; several of the larger systems here (Sol-Ark, Victron's MultiPlus-II, MidNite Solar's components, EG4, and the Tesla, Enphase and FranklinWH home batteries) are normally sold through installers or distributors at a price that varies by configuration, so no price is scored for them rather than guessed at. Battery cycle life and warranty length are pulled from each manufacturer's own product or warranty page; the two bare batteries are priced for the battery alone, so their per-watt-hour figure leaves out the controller and inverter they still need. A safety record comes from the US Consumer Product Safety Commission's saferproducts.gov recall database, searched by brand name and dated 2026; where a recall exists it is named precisely, including when it applies to a different model from the same company than the one listed here, and where none was found the exact search term is given rather than treating silence as proof of safety. One real distinction runs through this roster: Generac's PWRcell, the battery brand many people already know from Generac's generators, states on its own product page that it 'is not an off-grid system' and needs the grid, solar or a generator to recharge, unlike Sol-Ark, EG4 or a Victron-based build, each designed to run independently of the grid. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Price for the storage capacity you get
Battery cycle life and warranty length before it needs replacing
Easy to buy and set up without hiring a specialist
Actually runs without the grid, rather than needing it to recharge
CPSC recall record for fire or burn risk

products.name: Goal Zero Yeti PRO 4000
products.description: A 3,994Wh portable power station from Goal Zero, one of the oldest names in solar power stations. It is the most expensive unit per watt-hour in this roster, but carries the longest cycle rating of the portable options here.

economical.note: Goal Zero lists the Yeti PRO 4000 at $3,999.95 for 3993.6Wh of LiFePO4 capacity, close to $1.00 per watt-hour, the highest per-watt-hour price of any unit scored in this roster.

durability.note: Goal Zero states the Yeti PRO 4000 has a '4000+ cycle lifespan' with 'over 10 years of daily use' and a 5 year warranty.

accessibility.note: Goal Zero sells the Yeti PRO 4000 as a self-contained power station: no separate charge controller, inverter or installer is needed to start using it, only a wall outlet or solar panel to charge it.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database lists seven Goal Zero recalls when searched in October 2026. The most recent, dated August 20, 2026, covers about 46,200 YETI 3000X power stations after four reports of fire, overheating and smoking, fixed by a free firmware update. Earlier ones cover accessories, including Solar Series combiner cables (February 2025) and Yeti Link modules with EC8 cables (June 2024). None names the Yeti PRO 4000 listed here.

links.label: CPSC: Goal Zero combiner cable recall

products.name: EcoFlow Delta Pro
products.description: A 3.6kWh portable power station from EcoFlow, expandable to 25kWh with extra battery packs, and one of the more affordable LFP units per watt-hour in this roster.

economical.note: EcoFlow lists the base DELTA Pro unit at $1,899 for 3.6kWh of expandable capacity, close to $0.53 per watt-hour, cheaper per watt-hour than the Goal Zero Yeti PRO 4000.

durability.note: EcoFlow's product page says the LFP battery 'supports up to 10 years' of daily use and lists '3000+ charging cycles,' backed by a '5-Year Warranty' made up of a 3-year standard term plus a 2-year extension available on app registration.

accessibility.note: The DELTA Pro is sold as a complete portable power station with no separate installer required, only a wall outlet, car charger or solar panel to charge it.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database lists one EcoFlow recall, dated October 9, 2025: the DELTA Max 2000 (model EFD310), about 25,030 units, recalled after six reports of the power station catching fire and over $850,000 in property damage. The recall names the Delta Max 2000, a different model from the Delta Pro listed here.

products.name: EcoFlow RIVER 3
products.description: A small 245Wh power station, the cheapest and smallest unit in this roster, big enough for phones, small appliances or a few hours of essentials rather than a whole home.

economical.note: EcoFlow lists the RIVER 3 at $229.00 for 245Wh of capacity, the lowest price of any unit in this roster.

durability.note: EcoFlow's product page rates the LiFePO4 battery at '3000 cycles to 80% capacity,' translating to about 10 years of everyday use before capacity drops to 80 percent, but does not state a warranty length on this page.

accessibility.note: At 245Wh, the RIVER 3 is small enough to carry and plug in immediately, with no installation of any kind.

products.name: Bluetti AC200MAX
products.description: A 2,048Wh power station from Bluetti, expandable to 8,192Wh with extra battery modules, sold at a mid-range price with the shortest stated warranty of the portable units here.

economical.note: Bluetti's own page lists the AC200MAX at a current sale price of $1,199.00, marked down from $1,699.00, for 2,048Wh, close to $0.59 per watt-hour at the sale price.

durability.note: Bluetti states the AC200MAX uses a 'LiFePO4 Battery with 3,500+ Life Cycles to 80%' and a '4-Year Hassle-Free Warranty,' the shortest warranty term of the portable power stations scored in this roster.

accessibility.note: The AC200MAX is a self-contained power station, expandable with extra battery modules but usable straight out of the box with no installer.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Bluetti' in 2026.

products.name: Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus
products.description: A 2,042Wh LiFePO4 power station from Jackery, one of the best-known portable power brands and the one most people already recognize, even though its own product page gave little detail beyond capacity when checked here.

accessibility.note: Jackery's own product page names the Explorer 2000 Plus a 'Portable Power Station' with '2042Wh Capacity' and a LiFePO4 battery, sold as a complete unit rather than a component to be installed.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Jackery' in 2026.

products.name: Anker SOLIX F3800
products.brand: large electronics brand's power station line
products.description: A 3,840Wh power station from Anker's SOLIX line, expandable to 53.8kWh with extra batteries, built around fast solar charging and a long-cycle battery Anker calls 'EV-grade.'

durability.note: Anker's tech specs list '3,000+ cycles' on 'LFP' chemistry described as 'EV-grade' with '10+ years of lifespan,' backed by a 5 year warranty.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Anker SOLIX' in 2026. A broader search for 'Anker' alone returns an unrelated recall for a different company's baby bath seat, which is not connected to Anker or SOLIX.

products.name: Sol-Ark 15K-2P
products.description: A 15kW all-in-one hybrid inverter built for whole-home off-grid, grid-tied or battery-backup use, normally installed by a professional rather than bought off the shelf.

environment.note: Sol-Ark's own page for the 15K-2P describes 'Grid-Down Generation' that lets the system 'continue generating power independently from the grid during prolonged power outages or blackouts,' delivering 15,000W of AC output and 12,000W from batteries alone.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Sol-Ark' in 2026, though a whole-home hybrid inverter this size is normally installed by a licensed electrician rather than sold as a standalone consumer product to begin with.

products.name: Victron Energy MultiPlus-II
products.description: An inverter/charger from the Dutch manufacturer Victron Energy, sold across a range of sizes from 3kVA to 15kVA and positioned for professional marine, vehicle and land-based off-grid installs rather than a plug-and-play consumer product.

durability.note: Victron's own MultiPlus-II page points to its 'industry-leading 5-year standard warranty and global repair service'.

accessibility.note: Victron markets the MultiPlus-II as 'suitable for professional marine, yachting, vehicle, and land-based off-grid systems,' language aimed at installers and system integrators rather than a buyer setting it up alone.

environment.note: Victron says the MultiPlus-II uses 'a smart adaptive algorithm that extends battery life' during charging, and switches to inverter power in under 20 milliseconds when grid or generator power is disconnected.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Victron' in 2026.

products.name: Generac PWRcell 2
products.description: A home battery system from Generac, the brand most US homeowners already know from fuel generators. Generac's own page for PWRcell 2 states plainly that it is not built to run a home independent of the grid.

durability.note: Generac's PWRcell 2 page states the system carries a '10 years' warranty on its components, and offers 9 to 18kWh per battery cabinet, up to 36kWh with two cabinets stacked.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results for 'PWRcell' specifically in 2026; a broader search for 'Generac' does return active recalls for other Generac product lines, such as electric-start pressure washers, which shows the database does cover the brand and the absence for PWRcell is not simply an unindexed name.

products.name: MidNite Solar Classic MPPT
products.description: An MPPT charge controller, one component of a self-built off-grid system rather than a complete unit, sold to be paired with a separate inverter and battery bank chosen by the buyer.

accessibility.note: MidNite markets the Classic as 'NORTH AMERICA'S MOST SOPHISTICATED MPPT CHARGE CONTROLLER,' with Ethernet, USB and RS232 monitoring and '20 megs of data logging,' a component for someone assembling their own system rather than a plug-and-play unit.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'MidNite' in 2026.

products.name: EG4 6000XP
products.description: A 6kW all-in-one off-grid inverter popular in the DIY off-grid community, taking up to 8kW of solar input and able to run split-phase on its own or paired with grid or generator input.

environment.note: EG4's own product page calls the 6000XP an 'All-In-One Off-Grid Inverter' and describes it as 'a 48V split-phase inverter/charger, providing powerful and efficient off-grid energy solutions', with 8kW of PV input and 6kW of output.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'EG4' in 2026.

products.name: Hire a NABCEP-certified installer
products.description: Paying a certified professional to design, size and install a custom off-grid system rather than choosing a product yourself. NABCEP is the credentialing body most of the industry recognizes for this work.

accessibility.note: NABCEP, a nonprofit certification body founded in 2002, says it gives consumers 'a way to hold unethical installers accountable' through an enforceable Code of Ethics, and lists certified professionals in a public directory, so a buyer with no technical background can find and vet an installer rather than needing to design a system alone.

products.name: Staying on the electric grid
products.description: Not buying an off-grid system at all: for a property the electric grid already reaches, staying connected is usually the cheapest way to keep the lights on, and needs nothing installed.

economical.note: University of Wyoming Extension's comparison of rural power options found utility line extension typically costs about $20,000 a mile to build new, but also lists a utility fixed charge above $265 a year as one signal that switching away from an existing connection pays off, which by the same logic means a property already paying less than that to stay connected is hard to beat on cost.

accessibility.note: There is nothing to buy, size or install: a property already wired to the grid keeps its power by doing nothing.

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus
products.description: A 1,024Wh LFP power station from EcoFlow, a smaller and newer sibling of the DELTA Pro already in this roster, that can be expanded with EcoFlow's extra battery packs and charged from two solar inputs.

economical.note: EcoFlow's own page lists the DELTA 3 Plus at a sale price of $719, marked down from $799, for 1,024Wh, close to $0.70 per watt-hour at the sale price: cheaper than the Goal Zero Yeti PRO 4000 per watt-hour but dearer than the DELTA Pro, Bluetti or Jackery units here.

durability.note: EcoFlow's spec table lists a cycle life of '4000 cycles to 80+% capacity' on LFP (LiFePO4) cells and a warranty of 5 years.

accessibility.note: Sold as a self-contained power station weighing about 27.6 lb, with six AC outlets and 1500W wall charging: nothing has to be wired or installed before it is used.

environment.note: The spec table lists two solar charging ports, '11V-60V 500W Max*2', so the unit can be recharged from panels with no grid connection; at 1,024Wh it covers essentials rather than a whole home.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned one EcoFlow recall when searched in October 2026: the DELTA Max 2000 power station (October 2025), a different model from the DELTA 3 Plus listed here. No recall names the DELTA 3 Plus.

products.name: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2
products.description: A 1,070Wh LiFePO4 power station from Jackery, the brand's mid-size model and one of the most widely sold units of its size, often bundled with a folding SolarSaga panel.

economical.note: Jackery's own page lists the Explorer 1000 v2 at $499.00, marked down from $559.00, for 1,070Wh, close to $0.47 per watt-hour, among the lower per-watt-hour prices in this roster.

durability.note: Jackery's tech specs list '4000 cycles to 70%+ capacity', a lower end-of-life threshold than the 80% most rivals here quote, and a '3+2 Years' warranty; the page's FAQ explains this as 3 years standard and 2 years extended, given only on units bought from Jackery or authorised sellers.

accessibility.note: Sold as a complete power station weighing around 23.8 lb, the lightest 1kWh-class unit in this roster, ready to use from the box.

environment.note: Jackery sells the unit bundled with its SolarSaga 200W panel as a 'Solar Generator 1000 v2', and the spec table lists two 8mm DC input ports, which the page's own FAQ describes connecting solar panels to, so it can recharge with no grid at all.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Jackery' in October 2026.

products.name: Bluetti AC180
products.description: A 1,152Wh LiFePO4 power station from Bluetti, the smaller sibling of the AC200MAX in this roster, sold at one of the lowest per-watt-hour prices of any complete unit here.

economical.note: Bluetti's own page lists the AC180 at $499.00 for 1,152Wh, close to $0.43 per watt-hour, the lowest per-watt-hour price of the complete power stations in this roster.

durability.note: Bluetti states '3,500+ Cycles to 80% Original Capacity' and a '5-year Hassle Free Warranty', one year longer than the AC200MAX's warranty.

accessibility.note: A self-contained unit weighing 35.3 lb with four 120V outlets, used straight out of the box with no installer.

environment.note: Bluetti's comparison table lists a 500W maximum solar input, and the page title names four recharging ways, AC, solar, car and generator, so it can be kept charged from panels alone.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Bluetti' in October 2026.

products.name: Anker SOLIX C1000
products.brand: large electronics brand's power station line
products.description: A 1,056Wh LFP power station from Anker's SOLIX line, expandable with one extra battery to 2,112Wh. Anker has recalled other battery products, though not this one.

economical.note: Anker's own page lists the C1000 at $469.99 after a $130 saving, for 1,056Wh, close to $0.45 per watt-hour; some bundles on the same page were marked sold out when checked, the base unit was not.

durability.note: Anker's page lists 'LFP batteries with 3,000 Cycles and 5-year hassle-free warranty', the same cycle rating and warranty length as EcoFlow's DELTA Pro here.

accessibility.note: Sold as a complete power station weighing 28.44 lb, with 11 ports, needing no installation.

environment.note: Anker states the C1000 offers 'up to 600W Fast Solar Recharging, fully powering the device in just 1.8 hours', so it can run and recharge with no grid connection.

safety.note: CPSC lists several Anker recalls for other battery products, none of them the C1000 or any SOLIX power station. The largest, in June 2025, covered about 1,158,000 Anker PowerCore 10000 power banks (model A1263) after 19 reports of fires and explosions. A search for 'Anker SOLIX' on saferproducts.gov returns nothing.

links.label: CPSC: Anker power bank recall, June 2025

products.name: Renogy Core Mini 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 battery
products.description: A 12.8V, 100Ah lithium iron phosphate battery from Renogy, a common building block of DIY van, cabin and shed systems. It stores power cheaply but is only a battery: a charge controller, inverter and panels have to be chosen and wired separately.

economical.note: Renogy lists the 100Ah Core Mini at $307.99 for a single battery, about 1,280Wh at 12.8V, close to $0.24 per watt-hour: the cheapest storage per watt-hour in this roster, but before the controller, inverter and wiring a complete system needs.

durability.note: Renogy's spec table lists '5000 Cycles (80% DOD, 80% EOL)' and a '5-year prorated material and workmanship warranty': a long cycle rating, but a prorated warranty pays out less the older the battery is.

accessibility.note: Renogy sells this as a bare 12V battery with terminal bolts and a manual, to be wired in series or parallel (up to 4S4P) into a system the buyer designs; nothing on the page makes it usable on its own. The page claims 'UL, FCC, and CE certified', but the certifications row of the same spec table lists no UL standard.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Renogy' in October 2026.

products.name: Battle Born 100Ah 12V LiFePO4 battery
products.description: A 12V, 100Ah lithium iron phosphate battery assembled in Reno, Nevada, by Battle Born, a brand of the listed company Dragonfly Energy. It costs more than imported rivals and carries one of the longest warranties of any battery here.

economical.note: Battle Born lists the 100Ah 12V battery at $799.00, down from $949.00, about 1,280Wh at 12.8V nominal and close to $0.62 per watt-hour: more than twice the Renogy battery's price for the same capacity, again before controller and inverter.

durability.note: Battle Born rates the battery for a '3,000–5,000 Cycle Lifespan' and backs it with a 10-year warranty, twice the term of most batteries and power stations in this roster.

accessibility.note: Sold as a drop-in replacement for a lead-acid battery, to be wired into a system with its own charger and inverter; the page says it is 'trusted by installers and OEM manufacturers' and lists NRTL safety listings including UL 2054 and UL 1642.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Battle Born' in October 2026; a search for its parent 'Dragonfly' returned only unrelated recalls for a stroller and an insect trap.

products.name: Tesla Powerwall 3
products.description: A 13.5kWh whole-home battery with a built-in solar inverter, sold and installed only through Tesla or its certified installers. Its predecessor, Powerwall 2, was recalled for overheating in 2025.

durability.note: Tesla's current US Powerwall limited warranty covers Powerwall 3 for ten years against defects and guarantees '70% at 10 years following initial installation date' with 'Unlimited cycles' when used for solar self-consumption, time-based control or backup; any other use, which would include running fully off grid, is capped at 37.8 MWh of throughput.

accessibility.note: The warranty applies only to a Powerwall bought 'from Tesla or a Tesla certified installer' and installed in the US: it is not a product a buyer installs alone.

safety.note: CPSC recalled about 10,500 Tesla Powerwall 2 units in November 2025 after 22 reports of overheating, including six of smoking and five of fire; Tesla remotely discharged affected units that were online. The recall names Powerwall 2, the predecessor of the Powerwall 3 listed here, and no recall names Powerwall 3.

products.name: Enphase IQ Battery 5P
products.description: A 5kWh modular home battery from Enphase, the US microinverter maker, stacked in multiples and installed as part of an Enphase solar system. It carries the longest cycle warranty in this roster.

durability.note: Enphase's store page says the IQ Battery 5P 'is covered by a 15-year limited warranty up to 6,000 cycles' on lithium iron phosphate cells, the longest term and highest warrantied cycle count of any battery in this roster.

accessibility.note: The page describes a battery that 'installers can quickly design' into a system and that provides backup only 'when installed with IQ System Controller 3/3G'; its listed modes are 'backup, self-consumption, and time of use (TOU) modes', with no off-grid mode named.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'Enphase' in October 2026.

products.name: FranklinWH aPower 2
products.description: A 15kWh whole-home battery with a 10kW inverter from FranklinWH, stackable to 225kWh and, unlike several home batteries here, stated by its maker to be built to run a home off the grid.

durability.note: FranklinWH's datasheet, dated October 2026, lists a '15-year or 60 MWh throughput warranty' on lithium iron phosphate cells, matching Enphase for the longest warranty term in this roster.

environment.note: The same datasheet says 'The system is off-grid ready, designed to operate independently from the main power grid', and gives a separate table of off-grid specifications.

safety.note: CPSC's saferproducts.gov database returned no results when searched for 'FranklinWH' in October 2026; a broader search for 'Franklin' returns only recalls for unrelated companies, such as Franklin Sports and Franklin Electric.
